# Climate downscaling using diffusion models

## 1. Introduction
Climate downscaling, transforming a coarse-resolution climate field to a high-resolution climate field, has
gained significance under a changing climate (Ling et al., 2024). A high-resolution
climate field can represent local extremes on a fine scale, giving authorities the opportunity to allocate
their resources more precisely (Addison et al., 2022).

-- In the past decades many different statistics or ML appraoches have been applied to downscaling.
-- A new approach in this context is using diffusion models (Song?) usually used in the context of text-to-image 
or superesolution tasks for this downscaling. 
-- An often cited advantage is that it is computatinally cheaper to downscale climate fields using diffusion models
as well as that you can generate ensembles of high-resolution climate fields from a coarse-resolution climate field
reflecting the uncertainty in weather/climate data.
-- Past papers such as (Mardani/WM etc) have used diffusion models in this downscaling context, but they mostly did this
in reanalysis context (what is reanalysis data => historical data), what might be an interesting caveat is to 
assess how a model trained on reanalysis/historical data behaves on climate projection data aka on data coming from a
different distributions, thus assessing how well the model is able to generalize in its downscaling capabilities to
unseen climate scenarios.
